title: EMULATE_FUNCTION_POINTER_CASTS and WASM=1
body:
I'm trying to build Python with Numpy as part of iodide-project/iodide, an in-browser scientific computing notebook.

I have something that largely works with `asm.js`, but when I turn on `WASM=1` it fails to compile, spewing many wasm validation errors.  Output from the build is available [here](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iodide-project/pyodide-demo/master/build.log) (85MB) Is this a known issue?

To reproduce, check out the `numpy` branch of iodide-project/pyodide, and edit the `Makefile` to add `-s WASM=1`.  You'll also need to apply my small patch to emscripten in #6308.
comments:
[kripken]: Hmm, something definitely looks wrong here :) Thanks for filing!

First I opened https://github.com/WebAssembly/binaryen/pull/1463 for all those warnings. The PR should at least limit the amount shown.

Looking in the errors, it all seems to be fp emulation stubs that return a float and receive an integer, and don't bother to cast it. Strange that that doesn't work. Can you send me the `.asm.js` file, which is the input to the asm2wasm invocation that shows those errors? (if you build with `EMCC_DEBUG=1` in the env, it will save that file locally, or maybe just in `/tmp/emscripten_temp/` since it fails)

Also worrying in that output is that e.g. `_unicode_upper` is called with no param from all the fp emulation stubs. Then asm2wasm adds a zero to get validation to work (causing all those warnings). But the question is why it didn't send a parameter anyhow, so maybe those warnings are in fact indicating real problems. Looking in the `.asm.js` file may clear that up too.

---

[kripken]: Actually, no need for the .asm.js file, I see I can reproduce this just by running the python test in the test suite, if I add `MAIN_MODULE=1`.

Still investigating, but definitely something wrong here, we have e.g. `instance_dealloc` take one param and return nothing, but the emulation functions look like
```
function fpemu_i_17() {
 ; return _instance_dealloc()|0
}
[..]
function fpemu_ii_17(p0) {
 p0 = p0|0; return _instance_dealloc()|0
}
```

---

[kripken]: The issue is that `EMULATED_FUNCTION_POINTERS` in wasm mode puts all the functions in one table, discarding the asm.js type info. We used that info to set up the fpemu functions, and silently got meaningless data. Not sure yet how to fix this.

---

[kripken]: Investigating, there isn't a trivial fix for this. The asm.js backend would just need to be improved to also emit metadata about function types for each function, and emscripten.py would need to parse that when computing `function_pointer_targets`.

Would be good to fix, but on the other hand asm.js does work with this currently, and in the long term wasm dynamic linking will probably change anyhow, so fixing this for wasm now would just be of temporary benefit, I think.

---

[kripken]: Actually maybe we can just parse the types out of the asm.js. I'll look into that.

---

[aheejin]: Not sure if this is relevant, but we are generating type signature information from wasm backend for `addFunction` support now. [Here](https://github.com/WebAssembly/binaryen/blob/be9243419302aca1ff088004546205f1c252f9c5/test/dot_s/reserved_func_ptrs.jscall.wast#L281) is an example metadata and [here](https://github.com/WebAssembly/binaryen/blob/be9243419302aca1ff088004546205f1c252f9c5/src/wasm-emscripten.cpp#L246-L298) is the function that generates it. Can we do something similar?

---

[kripken]: @aheejin hmm, yeah, it's much more practical to find the signature in binaryen. Doing this in binaryen would also mean it works in the wasm backend. So that's a good idea.

But I'm actually not sure it can be done well at that level. The core problem in function pointer cast emulation is that we indirectly call a function `f` which has type `t` but the indirect call itself statically has type `u`. So we need to match up the number of parameters and their types (dropping extra ones, adding a zero of the right type for missing ones, etc.).

In asm.js, we have a separate function table for each type. For a particular index, normally all of the tables contain NULL, except for the table with the right type. In emulation mode we replace those NULLs with thunks that statically fix things up. So indexes don't need to change. And the overhead isn't too bad actually, just an extra direct call basically.

In wasm we just have a single table, though. If the table were of a fixed size then we could add an offset for each type, maybe, but assuming a fixed size would rule out dynamic linking which is the motivation in this issue here actually.

Another option might be to spill params to globals or the stack. Then the thunk could unspill them, add missing ones and ignore unneeded ones, and do the call. Seems like that could work but I worry it would be quite slow...

---

[kripken]: Or, maybe we can limit the number of parameters, and have all indirect calls use the full number of them with i64, and the thunks would translate to the right thing for the target. That seems not terribly slow, so it could be good enough. I'll try it.

---

[kripken]: Ok, I implemented this in `fcastemu` branches in binaryen and emscripten. It fixes the case of python in the test suite with `MAIN_MODULE`, which should mean it also fixes the original testcase here. Still running tests on CI though, will open PRs when this looks fully correct.

---

[kripken]: Those branches landed so this should now be all fixed.

title: WebAssembly: wrong conversion from double to int64 when OUTLINING_LIMIT isn't 0
body:
The result of the conversion from double to signed/unsigned int64 is wrong when OUTLINING_LIMIT is non-zero.

Having the following code:
```
#include <iostream>
#include <cmath>

int64_t __attribute__ ((noinline)) toSInteger64(double x) {
  return (int64_t)x;
}

int main(int argc, char ** argv) {    
    double a = 1520968721803.0;
    int64_t b = toSInteger64(a);
    std::cout << "result: " << b << std::endl;
    return 0;
}
```
If compile it without setting `OUTLINING_LIMIT` (or setting it to zero) everything is ok:
```
emcc \
    -s WASM=1 \
    -s OUTLINING_LIMIT=0 \
    -g0 -g\
    -w --emrun \
    hello.cpp -o hello.html 
```
`emrun ./hello.html`
>result: 1520968721803

If set some `OUTLINING_LIMIT` and pass `"BINARYEN_TRAP_MODE='clamp'"` the result is wrong:
```
emcc \
    -s "BINARYEN_TRAP_MODE='clamp'" \
    -s WASM=1 \
    -s OUTLINING_LIMIT=100000 \
    -g0 -g\
    -w --emrun \
    hello.cpp -o hello.html
```
`emrun ./hello.html`
>result: 1522565906432

If set some `OUTLINING_LIMIT` and do not set `"BINARYEN_TRAP_MODE='clamp'"` the exception is raised:
```
emcc \
    -s WASM=1 \
    -s OUTLINING_LIMIT=100000 \
    -g0 -g\
    -w --emrun \
    hello.cpp -o hello.html
```
`emrun ./hello.html`
>exception thrown: Error: Out of bounds Trunc operation (evaluating 'Module["asm"]["_main"].apply(null, arguments)'),wasm function: __Z12toSInteger64d@[wasm code]
>wasm function: _main@[wasm code]
>wasm function@[wasm code]
>_main@[native code]

Although as far as I can see setting OUTLINING_LIMIT when compiling to wasm is rather useless (correct me if I'm wrong) it is still quite unexpected behavior.
comments:
[kripken]: This is a tricky problem with conversions. Normally this works in wasm-only mode since we directly handle double->i64 conversions. However, when outlining or something else disables wasm-only mode, we have no i64s, and end up doing double->i32 conversions. Then the clamp mode matters.

As you saw, without clamping or anything we trap (the double is too big for an i32). With clamping, we clamp it to zero, giving the invalid result for the low bits. If you use the `js` mode `"BINARYEN_TRAP_MODE='js'"` it will work, since it copies the JS behavior exactly.

Not sure we should do anything here - in general wasm-only mode is more important anyhow. In theory we could do the double->i32 cast in a emulated way which would be much slower, but that's sort of what the `js` mode is for anyhow. Perhaps we should document this better, though?

---

[GraDKh]: Big thank for the answer. As for me - it was quite unexpected that the arithmetic works in a so unexpected way. When reading about trap mode I thought that it is about corner cases - overflows in the C++ sense. But now I see that asm.js type model matters, even if WebAsembly has single operands to do such conversion. It would be very nice to have this moment explained in documentation.
Also do I understand right that outlining doesn't improve the performance of WebAssembly build in general case? If yes it may be reasonable to produce a warning during compilation in this case.

---

[kripken]: Yeah, outlining isn't really needed in wasm, as VMs should be able to handle big functions well anyhow. I agree a warning makes sense there, I opened #6371 for that.

Maybe you can look into improving the docs for the trap mode issue? If you looked somewhere and didn't find an explanation there, that's probably the right place to mention this.

---

[GraDKh]: > Yeah, outlining isn't really needed in wasm, as VMs should be able to handle big functions well anyhow. I agree a warning makes sense there, I opened #6371 for that.

There is a more generic question: is there any sense to make any optimizations that disable wasm-only mode if targeting WebAssembly? Or we can say that in wasm-only code the resulting WebAssembly code will always be better?

> Maybe you can look into improving the docs for the trap mode issue? If you looked somewhere and didn't find an explanation there, that's probably the right place to mention this.

Yes for sure. But I'm not quite sure if my edits would be good enough and preserve the sense. Is there a possibility to make a somewhat like pull request to [https://github.com/kripken/emscripten/wiki/WebAssembly](url)?

---

[kripken]: >  is there any sense to make any optimizations that disable wasm-only mode if targeting WebAssembly

Hmm, good question. In theory that should only be done due to current limitations, like the emterpreter, outlining, etc. that are asm.js optimizer passes. Outlining happens to be not important for wasm, but the emterpreter is. But, eventually we should have something with emterpreter functionality for wasm-only.

> Is there a possibility to make a somewhat like pull request to https://github.com/kripken/emscripten/wiki/WebAssembly?

Is that not publicly editable? In any case, we should probably migrate that from the wiki into the main docs under `site/` since it's pretty stable and official now, and might as well use the normal PR methods on it etc.

[GraDKh]: > Is that not publicly editable? In any case, we should probably migrate that from the wiki into the main docs under site/ since it's pretty stable and official now, and might as well use the normal PR methods on it etc.

Yes, it's publicly editable. I've just wondered about the mechanism of reviewing my changes since I'm not sure if I'll describe everything right and the English will be of a good quality :)

I opened #6418 about moving that page from the wiki. Hopefully someone will want to do that soon.

In the short term for that wiki page, if you aren't sure of your edits, we can discuss them here first perhaps?

[reybits]: Documentation mentions
> WebAssembly can trap on rounding a very large float to an int

I have code that always traps:
```
    size_t getZoneIndex(const ageVector& pos) const
    {
        const auto x = (size_t)pos.x / ZoneSize;
        const auto y = (size_t)pos.y / ZoneSize;

        const auto idx = x + y * m_zoneCols;
        return idx;
    }
```

And no traps in debug mode or when I add logging:
```

    {
        my_log_like_printf("%g x %g\n", pos.x, pos.y);
        const auto x = (size_t)pos.x / ZoneSize;
        const auto y = (size_t)pos.y / ZoneSize;

        const auto idx = x + y * m_zoneCols;
        return idx;
    }
```

Where:

```
const size_t ZoneSize = 250;

struct ageVector
{
   float x;
   float y;
};
```

and `ageVector& pos` range is 0.0f - 7500.0f.

I try compile with Emscripten 1.38.1 and 1.38.5.

---

[reybits]: My ugly workaround is:
```
        const auto x = pos.x / ZoneSize;
        const auto y = pos.y / ZoneSize;

        const auto idx = (size_t)x + (size_t)y * m_zoneCols;
```

---

[kripken]: @andreyugolnik I assume that is without setting the trap mode to clamp? That might be a good solution (if it doesn't work, please let us know).

---

[reybits]: @kripken thank you for reply.
I doesn't set any trap mode. As I know this means `allow` trap mode by default.
I will try `-s "BINARYEN_TRAP_MODE='clamp'"` option.

comments:
[kripken]: Any chance you can provide the input bitcode, to reproduce the problem?

Without that, as best I can guess is that since the crash is on
```
assert(foundAsmLibraryArgAssign); // must find the info we need
```
then something altered the JS that sets up the wasm imports, into a form we can't recognize. None of your compiler flags seems obviously related to that. Perhaps try removing them, and see if compilation doesn't fail without one of them?

---

[mbasso]: > Any chance you can provide the input bitcode, to reproduce the problem?

Sure, I've just created a [repository called emscripten-issue-6442](https://github.com/mbasso/emscripten-issue-6442). It contains the `prefix.js`, `postfix.js` and two input files, one created using emscripten@1.37.22 (`input-1_37_22.bc`) and another created using emscripten@1.37.36 (`input-1_37_36.bc`). I don't know if it can be useful but I've put both in the repo... I've also written a Makefile with 2 commands to test it more easily.
I've created these files from [asm-dom](https://github.com/mbasso/asm-dom) project, from branch `0.6.0`, but there is the same problem on `master`.

> Perhaps try removing them, and see if compilation doesn't fail without one of them?

I've tried to remove some params... It seems that there's a problem with `prefix.js` and `postfix.js`, `emcc` compiles them correctly with `-O2` but gives and error with `-O3`. Running the command without them and `-O3` all works fine

---

[kripken]: Thanks! Ok, I see the problem here: your pre/post js files put all the code inside a function scope. But that pass expects the emscripten output to be at the top level.

This is definitely not clear in our current docs, and maybe not even in our thinking. But I think we should document this as not what pre/post-js are meant for: the idea with those options is code to add to emscripten to be optimized with the rest of its output. That's different from code that could have been prepended/appended after emscripten runs, that the optimizer doesn't need to know about. But this is a little subtle... hard to document, and harder to provide a better error message for. But maybe we can figure that out.

Separately, I think our MODULARIZE and MODULARIZE_INSTANCE options can achieve what your pre/post-jses do, maybe you can use one of those?

---

[kripken]: An improvement for the error message is in #6444, but I'd like to find even more to do here, this is confusing stuff.

---

[mbasso]: Awesome! Thank you.

> Separately, I think our MODULARIZE and MODULARIZE_INSTANCE options can achieve what your pre/post-jses do, maybe you can use one of those?

I think that I'll try to use `MODULARIZE` or `MODULARIZE_INSTANCE` with a new postfix.
I basically need to export the `Module` using AMD, CommonJS, Node.js or just as global, but I haven't find a feature that allows me to do that in a different way.

> An improvement for the error message is in #6444, but I'd like to find even more to do here, this is confusing stuff.

Do you think that `MODULARIZE` and `MODULARIZE_INSTANCE` might export the module directly using these standards? A library built with emscripten and usable from JavaScript probably needs it. This means, for example, that we can use the generated code with [webpack](https://webpack.js.org/) without problems. Also, prefix and postfix will be used for other purposes.
What do you think about it? I can open another issue if that makes sense

---

[kripken]: I don't know enough about AMD, CommonJS etc. myself, but I know there have been some discussions about them. It would be good to support them out of the box if that's possible. Maybe search through the issues a little for those terms, and if there isn't an obvious existing issue, open a new one?

---

[curiousdannii]: Emscripten already makes CommonJS exports, both with and without MODULARIZE. With MODULARIZE it will also do an AMD export.

---

[mbasso]: Hi @curiousdannii,
yes, I've just found [this](https://github.com/kripken/emscripten/pull/6006) PR, but it seems that there is no reference to CommonJS and AMD in the doc (I've read the `MODULARIZE` option in `settings.js`). Do you think that we have to update the doc to make it clearer?

---

[curiousdannii]: A PR for the docs would surely help. (Until recently Modularize was hardly even mentioned, I think it was hidden somewhere odd like WebIDL.)

---

[kripken]: Good idea, renamed this issue to focus on improving those docs.

---

[rajsite]: Hmm interesting, hit the same thing trying out the WASM=1 flag after upgrading to 1.37.36. Based on the updated docs in #6444 sounds like our usage was unexpected as well: https://github.com/ni/VireoSDK/blob/master/source/core/vireo.wrapper.js#L30

(we have a script to split that file during build to create a pre and post js)

The thing that I'm not a fan of with the current MODULARIZE=1 behavior is that it exposes globally a way to construct the Emscripten Module instance when I would prefer to wrap that privately and give a better API for users. Is the best way to support that by modifying the generated .js file after build as suggested in the [MODULARIZE](https://github.com/kripken/emscripten/blob/40584e0e4f65c2ad5056a5b4f6916934e7f4957a/src/settings.js#L595) doc?

---

[kripken]: Yes, modifying it or wrapping it after emcc runs is the best way to do that.

I hope we can find a way to make this more clear and natural. How about if we had 4 options,

 * `--pre-js`, `--post-js`
 * `--external-pre-js`, `--external-post-js`

where the first two are "internal" and optimized with the main output, and the last two are "external" and added after all optimization? This would let us refer people to the `--external-*` options when relevant.

I worry though that adding more options might make it more confusing...

---

[curiousdannii]: I think it would be better to just recommend people use Browserify or Webpack. And in the future make MODULARIZE be on by default.

Ideal changes IMO (would be breaking changes):

 - MODULARIZE on by default
 - Fix #5820, probably through returning a real promise
 - Possibly remove `onRuntimeInitialized` so as to reduce redundant alternatives
 - Add a flag to switch from UMD to ES6 module exports #6284

---

[mbasso]: > Fix #5820, probably through returning a real promise

I've just faced this issue too and I had to manually delete `.then` to resolve a Promise with the instance of my library:

```js
import('../library.js').then(Module => {
    const lib = Module(config);
    delete lib.then;
    return lib;
});
```

> MODULARIZE on by default

I think that it would be great to enable it by default, new users would be ready to use the generated code without configuration

> I worry though that adding more options might make it more confusing...

Maybe we can use `--pre-js`, `--post-js` and another option, let's say `---template-js <file>` with a placeholder? Something similar to https://github.com/ni/VireoSDK/blob/master/source/core/vireo.wrapper.js#L30

---

[kripken]: What's our current status with browserify and webpack - can those use emscripten output now? Or would we need to implement some sort of plugins for them?

Coincidentally I've started to work on a [webpack plugin for binaryen](https://github.com/kripken/binaryen-webpack-plugin), and am learning some npm and webpack as I go...

---

[curiousdannii]: It's safe if you use MODULARIZE. If you don't then Emscripten will only do a CommonJS export when ENVIRONMENT_IS_NODE is true (#5864). It should be changed to do a full UMD export unconditionally.

---

[kripken]: I see, thanks @curiousdannii. Yeah, we should definitely document that MODULARIZE is currently required for those.

I wonder if that isn't enough for us? That is, do you think it's worth getting non-MODULARIZE code working with webpack and browserify? Intuitively, I think they expect something like a module and so MODULARIZE being the way to integrate with them seems reasonable?

---

[curiousdannii]: We definitely should, and it won't be difficult. It's just a matter of moving and expanding these lines:

https://github.com/kripken/emscripten/blob/33afb86a5a4a2ea8cb0bd7c89f8f2af61aff9f27/src/shell.js#L128-L130

to look like these

https://github.com/kripken/emscripten/blob/56e1a9019dd1f3fe9917f0799aa2aa43f7688bad/emcc.py#L2480-L2485

I'll try to get a PR done soon.

In terms of what's expected, non-MODULARIZEd code is fine. After all, MODULARIZE is just adding a wrapping function, which is what Webpack and Browserify do anyway.

Hmm, just had a thought about MODULARIZE_INSTANCE. I haven't used it so I don't know all the rationale for it, but is there a good reason why it doesn't provide `.then()`? In my mind MODULARIZE_INSTANCE shouldn't really change anything, all it's doing is calling `Module()` for you, that's all. You can use `onRuntimeInitialized` in both for example. So why not also provide `.then`? (It would be possible to provide a `then` function without MODULARIZE, though I'd prefer we just make it the default instead.)

What would you think about making MODULARIZE be on by default as part of the major release that turns WASM on? IMO it usually makes sense to bundle changing defaults like this.

---

[kripken]: Well, a downside is that by adding those lines we make the default output larger. I think maybe requiring `MODULARIZE` be passed to indicate "I want to use this as a module" might make sense. But also maybe I'm overthinking this :)

About `MODULARIZE_INSTANCE` and `.then()`, yeah, it seems like we could support that, good idea.

About `MODULARIZE` on by default, I think that's worth considering, but I actually feel the opposite about bundling stuff - splitting big changes into separate releases lets people upgrade their projects more incrementally, and if something breaks the Changelog can help figure it out more easily with fewer changes per version.

---

[curiousdannii]: When we add the ES6 modules option that will be much more concise :) Fair enough on your other points.

---

title: SAFE_HEAP=1 breaks source map generation for WASM
body:
CMakeLists.txt
```
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 2.8)

project(cpp_with_emscripten_val)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 11)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

set(CMAKE_EXECUTABLE_SUFFIX ".html")

set(EMSCRIPTEN_FLAGS " -s WASM=1")
set(CMAKE_C_FLAGS             "${CMAKE_C_FLAGS} ${EMSCRIPTEN_FLAGS}")
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS           "${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS} ${EMSCRIPTEN_FLAGS}")
set(CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS    "${CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS} ${EMSCRIPTEN_FLAGS}")

set(EMSCRIPTEN_FLAGS_DEBUG "-g4")
#set(EMSCRIPTEN_FLAGS_DEBUG "-g4 SAFE_HEAP=1")
set(CMAKE_C_FLAGS_DEBUG "${CMAKE_C_FLAGS_DEBUG} ${EMSCRIPTEN_FLAGS_DEBUG}")
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUG "${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUG}  ${EMSCRIPTEN_FLAGS_DEBUG}")
set(CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_DEBUG "${CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_DEBUG} ${EMSCRIPTEN_FLAGS_DEBUG} --source-map-base http://localhost:6931/")

add_executable(cpp_with_emscripten_val main.cpp)
```

main.cpp
```
#include <stdio.h>

int main()
{
	int test_int = 5;
	printf("Hello! test int: %d, __cplusplus: %ld\n", test_int, __cplusplus);
}
```
finally emrun you code place main.cpp where browser will search it(or just edit 1 line in .map file)
and try to set break point with Firefox developer edition everything will work good
then uncomment string SAFE_HEAP=1 and recompile break point not work now
comments:
[kripken]: I think this is the same as #4224. Basically SAFE_HEAP uses the js optimizer, and optimizing the JS messes up source maps currently.

---

[newnon]: And where is no way to use SAFE_HEAP with source maps?

---

[kripken]: Yes, until that bug is fixed, I think it doesn't work. Although I'm not sure if it's broken entirely or just not as good.

---

[newnon]: May be emscripten compiler should write some warning about SAFE_HEAP & -g4 something like
"source maps can be corrupted if with safe heap enabled"? I spend whole day on this bug.

---

[kripken]: Good idea, yeah, we should emit a warning at compile time.

Before that, I'm not sure I fully understand the issue yet, though. Trying it now, compiling a single file I see the same source map emitted with and without `SAFE_HEAP`. So there must be something more to trigger the bug?

---

[newnon]: Yes thats the problem - you got same source map but different binary, because after source map generation where is extra step that post process wasm binary.

---

[kripken]: Oh ok, I guess I don't understand how that works well enough then. @yurydelendik, maybe you know this better?

---

[dschuff]: The safe heap transformation is just a Binaryen pass, right? Does it run after the source map is already emitted? (e.g. emit a binary and source map, then re-parse and modify the binary?)

---

[yurydelendik]: Any wasm binary transformation invalidates source map generated with it. (The JS source maps no different, once JS is changed -- source map needs to be re-created) An optimizer must transform source map along with code optimization (again similar to JS), or remove source map.

---

[kripken]: I see, thanks @dschuff and @yurydelendik - yes, safe-heap is a binaryen pass now. So what happens with source maps + safe-heap is (in asm2wasm)

 * `asm2wasm` to a wast (which contains comments for code locations), including optimizations.
 * `wasm-as` to convert that to a wasm + a source map
 * `wasm-opt` to run safe-heap on the wasm, which breaks the source map :(

Since we run optimizations in that first phase, it seems like we could just run extra passes then too, by adding that capability to asm2wasm.

I'm not sure how this would work with the wasm backend path, though. We do currently run `wasm-opt` for safe-heap at the end there, like `asm2wasm`, so it seems like we'd need to run it during `s2wasm` or `wasm-emscripten-finalize`, but I'm not sure how source maps fit in with those?

---

[yurydelendik]: wasm-dis has ability to ingest locations from source maps (see https://github.com/WebAssembly/binaryen/blob/7a8273ae2c1854b9840fc56a952e572f673bb10f/src/tools/wasm-dis.cpp#L53). will it be useful for other passes?

---

[kripken]: Thanks, yeah, based on that + discussion on irc, I think we just need to use that in wasm-opt. I'll look into it.

---

[kripken]: wip code in https://github.com/WebAssembly/binaryen/pull/1557

---

One option is to add malloc to `OK_TO_CALL_WHILE_ASYNC` in `tools/js-optimizer.js`. But I'm not sure offhand if that is ok to do. In general, it's ok to call say `memset` while async, as it just does some pure computation and is guaranteed to complete synchronously. That's generally true of malloc, except it does call `sbrk` when it needs to. Maybe just try adding malloc there, and see what happens, to start figuring this out?

[Beuc]: Thanks!
The abort is added by this part of js-optimizer.js:
```
        // add an assert in the prelude of the function
        var stats = getStatements(func);
        for (var i = 0; i < stats.length; i++) {

I don't know why SDL2's mousebutton handle triggered this and not the other events (which are similarly implemented AFAICS).

More importantly I didn't realize there were limitations on calling the main program during the emscripten_sleep(), typically during registered event callbacks (html5.h). I'm not sure what's the worst case scenario if sbrk() is called async.
Do I need to e.g. I ditch all the SDL2 DOM even callbacks, have the DOM events temporarily stored in a JS array, and process them when going back from emscripten_sleep() ?

---

[kripken]: I'm not sure - this is complicated. Been a while since I worked on this, so I may not remember all the details.

Overall, the "simple" case is you do an `emscripten_sleep` and wait for some XHR or other browser async event, and then you resume the compiled code. In that case, no compiled code runs during the sleep.

Now imagine that someone calls some compiled code (from JS) during that sleep. It's violating the program's assumptions of how code should execute - that sleep should behave like a synchronous operation, with nothing happening in the middle. For example
```
int global = 0;

int func() {
  global = 1;
  emscripten_sleep();
  return global;
}

int confuse() {
  global = 2;
}
```
Here `func` should return 1 (unless the program is multithreaded, which it is not). But if JS calls `confuse` during the sleep, that changes.

On the other hand, if you have an event handler like here, then you do want other code to run. Another example is coroutines.

Overall, I think we may want to add an option, `EMTERPRETIFY_ALLOW_EXEC_DURING_ASYNC` (or a better name). That -12 error could point to it, and it would make sense to enable it for event handlers and coroutines, but not by default. But, this needs more thought - not sure I have the time to get into it myself.

title: Invalid Enum error on glGetIntegerv(GL_VERTEX_ARRAY_BINDING,...) with Webgl 1.0
body:
I just stumbled upon this issue in the current ( 46afd23 ) version of emscripten.

glGetIntegerv(GL_VERTEX_ARRAY_BINDING, &aGLInt);

gives INVALID_ENUM in WebGL 1.0 contexts with OES_vertex_array_object present and activated.

This is not expected behaviour, as the rest of the VAO APIs are working correctly.

This seems to be because in

https://github.com/kripken/emscripten/blob/incoming/src/library_gl.js

#if USE_WEBGL2
case 0x85B5: // GL_VERTEX_ARRAY_BINDING
case 0x8919: // GL_SAMPLER_BINDING
case 0x8E25: // GL_TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_BINDING
#endif

--> only if WebGL2 is used the call is actually executed, but not if just the extension is present...
comments:
[kripken]: Interesting, thanks for filing. Indeed that constant is defined in WebGL2 but also in WebGl1 + that extension.

We should probably add it to the `automaticallyEnabledExtensions` list in `library_gl.js`, but would need to confirm that it has no downsides (see comment there).

Another option might be in the default of that switch (where it's present for WebGL2) to check if the context has that value defined at runtime.

cc @juj

---

[larsbohn]: Thanks for commenting - OES_vertex_array_object is part of automaticallyEnabledExtensions, which is good.

It's just the glGetIntegerv(GL_VERTEX_ARRAY_BINDING, ...) which does not care about the extension.

Regards,
Lars

---

[juj]: Thanks @larsbohn, fix in PR #7645.

title: Emterpreter and changing function names
body:
(Note: I tried sending this twice to the emscripten-discuss mailing list, and it was silently dropped each time... Not sure what it didn't like)

When compiling my RenPyWeb project, which use Emterpreter, I often get
errors about new, non-whitelisted functions such as:

  ___Pyx_PyObject_CallNoArg_387
  ___Pyx_PyObject_CallNoArg_6345

This may happen when I make some changes in the code or in the
compilation flags.

AFAIU these are generated by Emscripten ('grep' only sees references in
Emscripten-generated files) and the numbers are some kind of offset.

This is annoying because I usually have to compile (5-10mn depending on
target), run in a browser and wait for complete startup (couple
minutes), get the new stack strace, edit my Makefile and
EMTERPRETIFY_WHITELIST, and repeat.
And I need to tell my users/contributors to do the same 

Is there anything I can do to avoid these dynamic function names?
comments:
[kripken]: I think the source of those numbers is the linker - it adds suffixes when names would otherwise collide (e.g. two files might contain `static ___Pyx_PyObject_CallNoArg` so it has to differentiate them when linked together). I'm not sure how that works, but I guess it's not deterministic in a predictable way?

One option here may be to support wildcards in the whitelist, perhaps. Another is you can use `llvm-nm` on the final linked bitcode, to see what names it emitted, and can have a script in your build syste to generate the whitelist from that.

---

[Beuc]: Those are static conflicts indeed:
```
gen/pygame_sdl2.transform.c:static CYTHON_INLINE PyObject* __Pyx_PyObject_CallNoArg(PyObject *func);
```
```
$ for i in *.o; do echo -n $i:; llvm-nm $i|grep CallNoArg || echo; done
pygame_sdl2.color.o:-------- t __Pyx_PyObject_CallNoArg
pygame_sdl2.controller.o:-------- t __Pyx_PyObject_CallNoArg
...
pygame_sdl2.surface.o:-------- t __Pyx_PyObject_CallNoArg
pygame_sdl2.transform.o:-------- t __Pyx_PyObject_CallNoArg
```

I don't know how the number is computed. It's moderately stable (doesn't change everytime), it's not the line number, and it changes depending on other files linked and possibly the linker options used.

With a 2-steps compilation (*.bc -> monolith.bc -> .html), I can see some matching symbols (modulo "." -> "_"):
```
-------- t __Pyx_PyObject_CallNoArg
-------- t __Pyx_PyObject_CallNoArg.10863
-------- t __Pyx_PyObject_CallNoArg.1301
-------- t __Pyx_PyObject_CallNoArg.1847
-------- t __Pyx_PyObject_CallNoArg.2057
-------- t __Pyx_PyObject_CallNoArg.216
```
which I can crudely flag:
```
-s EMTERPRETIFY_WHITELIST='["_main", ... $(shell llvm-nm build/t/index.bc | grep -Po '__Pyx_PyObject_CallNoArg\.\d+' | sed -e 's/\./_/' -e 's/.*/"&"/' | tr '\n' ',') ...]'
```
(I had to LOL though ;))

One issue is I cannot distinguish which ones to whitelist (though in this particular case these functions are reasonably quick).
If we need to live with this imprecision, a wildcard makes more sense.

---

[kripken]: Heh, nice shell command :)

Yeah, +1 for a whitelist wildcard then.

---

[Beuc]: For reference my work-around is flawed - and I don't understand how it worked until I upgraded today...
Missing a leading '_', and not executed by 'make' at the right time.
```
-s EMTERPRETIFY_WHITELIST='["...", '`llvm-nm build/t/index.bc | grep -Po '__Pyx_PyObject_CallNoArg\.\d+' | sed -e 's/\./_/' -e 's/.*/"_&"/' | tr '\n' ','`' "..."]'
```

body:
It seems Node.js doesn't cache the compiled wasm binary by default (https://github.com/saschanaz/flif-wasm/issues/8, https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/18265).

So I want to use `v8.serialize` and `v8.deserialize` to cache it myself and pass it to emscripten JavaScript wrapper. Is it possible now?

Short deserialization example: https://runkit.com/saschanaz/5c84667c6e2ea0001222a59f
comments:

---

[saschanaz]: @sbc100 Agree, but not an option in current versions.

---

---

[sbc100]: Oh I see you already referenced the upstream bug.  Sorry for not reading that correctly.

---

[saschanaz]: That bug is about deserializing a manually cached binary.

It seems the browser devs want to do it [in HTTP cache level](https://github.com/WebAssembly/host-bindings/issues/16#issuecomment-425946581) rather than to do some magic in the `Module` constructor, which won't be helpful when the wasm file is in local.

title: LTO flags with wasm backend
body:
Discussing with @aardappel, a few things seem incomplete in our LTO support with the wasm backend. The only way it works right now is to pass `-s WASM_OBJECT_FILES=0` for each compilation to object, and also at link time, and to also add `--llvm-lto 1` at link time as well. However,

1. Perhaps `-flto` should turn on `-s WASM_OBJECT_FILES=0`?
2. Perhaps `--llvm-lto 1` should do the same? And also work when compiling to an object file?
3. Perhaps we should deprecate the `--llvm-lto 2/3` modes, as those don't work with the wasm backend - do we still want them? (they run more llvm opts than the standard llvm-link-opts)

A related issue is that building an object file with `-s WASM_OBJECT_FILES=0` and linking it without that flag will fail, I'm not sure if that's expected to work or not? E.g.

title: dynamicAlloc() doesn't work with memory growth
body:
Emscripten 1.38.31

main.c:
```C
int main() {
}
```
post.js:
```JavaScript
for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    var buf = getMemory(10000000);
    console.log(buf);
}
```

```shell
$ emcc -s ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH=1 main.c --post-js post.js -o out.js
$ node out.js
5246848
15246848
15246848
```
Note that second and third `getMemory()` calls return the same pointer.

This is because `dynamicAlloc()` doesn't update `HEAP32[DYNAMICTOP_PTR>>2]` when the heap is resized.

https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/blob/46a5d4672344d5d0704cfff9c968e6e49d47130d/src/support.js#L31-L42

It seems like a bug introduced by https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/pull/7897.

title: EXPORT_ES6 + USE_PTHREADS not compatible with ASSERTIONS
body:
Due to the changes introduced in #8306 EXPORT_ES6 now works with USE_PTHREADS. However I couldn't get the assertions for checking if the runtime is initialised to work in a worker.
There is an assertion added here:
https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/blob/1e5317c764fc94f736b7b38dd8a062f63d8e3308/emscripten.py#L1705
But without that it would throw with `TypeError: Cannot assign to read only property '${overwritten_property_name}' of object '[object Object]'`

As far as I can tell it's only that block of assertion that have trouble.

See this comment chain for more discussion: https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/pull/8306#discussion_r272006611
comments:

`receiving = "if (!ENVIRONMENT_IS_PTHREAD) {\n" + receiving + "}\n"`

I think a better solution is needed to fix this properly, but if someone desperately needs `EXPORT_ES6` + `USE_PTHREADS` + `ASSERTIONS`, then this should at least get things running.

title: EM_JS code fails when using upstream Clang
comments:
[cwoffenden]: Just to add, compiling the `EM_JS` code alone to a `.bc` doesn't fail, e.g.: `emcc test.c -o test.bc` followed by `emcc main.c test.bc -o out.html`.

The error is specifically when compiling all to a `.bc` then creating the wasm from that.

---

[jgravelle-google]: Looked at this with help from @sbc100

Of note is the .bc files as compiled with the upstream backend are, in fact, .o object files. To get actual bitcode, you can compile with `emcc main.c test.c -o out.bc -s WASM_OBJECT_FILES=0`, and this works.

This is why `test.bc` works, because it's really an object file. So that's equivalent to `emcc -c test.c -o test.o && emcc main.c test.o -o out.html`

The problem is a bug in the lld linker when merging two object files into another object file, and dropping the object visibility on the generated `__em_js__testjs` function, which keeps it from being DCE'd by the linker so wasm-emscripten-finalize can generate the metadata so emcc can create the `testjs` function in JS (whew).

Linking two object files together is a really unusual case, and you probably don't want to be doing it by accident. For a quick fix I'd say use `-s WASM_OBJECT_FILES=0` to keep generating actual bitcode. Long-term you'll want to build with `emcc -c main.c test.c` which will build main.o and test.o, which can be linked with `emcc main.o test.o -o out.html`. This is preferable because you get much faster incremental linking.

This sort of confusion makes me think we should tweak the "stopping at bitcode" logic (the actual message here is "stopping at object files"). Either make it always actual bitcode, or handle .bc and .o suffixes separately (e.g. .bc implies WASM_OBJECT_FILES=0 if not otherwise set), or at least only handle the object file suffixes we recognize (`emcc test.c -o test.fish` build a test.fish file that is also a wasm object file).

So tl;dr there are several workarounds, but also a bug in the linker.

---

[cwoffenden]: Thanks for the explanation. We were compiling to `.bc` with the old fastcomp because it let us half our 20 minute build time (compile the main project to `.bc` with some `.bc` libs for code that doesn't change much, then use that to make separate wasm them asm.js builds). Our current workaround is to just build twice.

With the new upstream Clang I'm assuming we'd build wasm then use `wasm2js` to create the asm.js equivalent. We've not tried this approach yet though.

---

[kripken]: @jgravelle-google - in your last comment it sounds like there's a bug in the linker. Do you know if there are any updates there (and is there a better bug filed for it)?

---

[jgravelle-google]: > The problem is a bug in the lld linker when merging two object files into another object file, and dropping the object visibility on the generated __em_js__testjs function, which keeps it from being DCE'd by the linker so wasm-emscripten-finalize can generate the metadata so emcc can create the testjs function in JS (whew).

Is the issue IIRC. I don't think there's any single bug for it; the general problem is that `wasm-ld a.o b.o -o c.o` is a very weird case that I don't think we have much support for. @sbc100 do you know of any tracking bugs for the linker emitting object files from object files?

---

[sbc100]: I assume you mean with `-r/--relocatable`?  It should work but perhaps we have found a bug here that we need to address.

---

[sbc100]: Oh I see now is the problem that visibility is not preserved with `--relocatable`.    No I don't think we have a bug for that yet.  I'll try to make a minimal repro case and open an llvm bug.

title: Out of bounds memory access with Os & BINARYEN_IGNORE_IMPLICIT_TRAPS=1
body:
Compiling the following program with 1.38.37 fastcomp using 
`emcc -Os -s BINARYEN_IGNORE_IMPLICIT_TRAPS=1 test.cpp -o test.js`
causes the program to misbehave and crash with
`RuntimeError: memory access out of bounds`

The optimizer removes the conditional surrounding the access to _dontAccess_ and merges it all into one block.

Here's the minimal repro code:
```
int len = 0;
unsigned* dontAccess = 0;

int main() {
   if (len == 0 || dontAccess[len - 1]) {
      len += 1;
   }
   return 0;
}
```

Omitting BINARYEN_IGNORE_IMPLICIT_TRAPS or changing the optimization level to e.g. O3 fixes it. 
Here's the WAST output of the working version. Notice the nested ifs.
```
func (result i32)
(local i32)
  i32.const 1024
  i32.load offset=0 align=4
  tee_local 0
  if <== CHECK IF LEN IS NON-ZERO AND AVOID ACCESSING THE ARRAY
    get_local 0
    i32.const -1
    i32.add
    i32.const 2
    i32.shl
    i32.load offset=0 align=4
    i32.eqz
    if
      i32.const 0
      return
    end
  end
  i32.const 1024
  get_local 0
  i32.const 1
  i32.add
  i32.store offset=0 align=4
  i32.const 0
end

```

Here's the WAST output from the failing case. The ifs have been flattened and both memory accesses always happen unconditionally (to _len_ and to the start of _dontAccess_) causing an invalid memory read.
```
func (result i32)
(local i32)
  i32.const 1024
  i32.load offset=0 align=4
  tee_local 0
  i32.eqz <== CHECK IF LEN IS ZERO 
  get_local 0
  i32.const -1
  i32.add
  i32.const 2
  i32.shl
  i32.load offset=0 align=4 <== THIS CRASHES
  i32.or <== NAIVELY OR THE RESULTS OF BOTH COMPARISONS
  if
    i32.const 1024
    get_local 0
    i32.const 1
    i32.add
    i32.store offset=0 align=4
  end
  i32.const 0
end
```

This does work with the latest upstream Clang 9 based Emscripten, but I think it's still worth investigating since the upstream doesn't seem to be read for prime time yet.
comments:
[sbc100]: Upstream clang should be ready for prime time now.  Please start using it if you can.

We are hoping to start the process of deprecating fastcomp as soon as possible.  For this reason I think its unlikely this will get fixed.

---

[kripken]: Yes, as @sbc100 said, [upstream should be ready now](https://v8.dev/blog/emscripten-llvm-wasm).

But going back to the testcase, this is actually that `BINARYEN_IGNORE_IMPLICIT_TRAPS` flag behaving as expected on fastcomp: it is ignoring the possible trap from the load, which allows it to compress the code more. But this code is exactly a case of where that option can lead to bad results.

So it's actually surprising that the wasm backend *doesn't* show the bug! Looking into that, there are 2 issues:

 * We forgot to pass the flag there :( fix in #8946 
 * The binaryen optimizer happens to not optimize the specific pattern seen here - in asm2wasm we have `br_if br_if`, which with the wasm backend it's `if br_if` - I'll look into adding support for that.

---

[tklajnscek]: First of all, thanks for the quick response guys!

We're definitely eager to switch to upstream, but still waiting on a few fixes before we go all in on it (e.g. #8905 & #8879).

As for the BINARYEN_IGNORE_IMPLICIT_TRAPS flag it was our understanding that it was about ignoring e.g. loads out of bounds that are not checked for and not emitting code that would handle those to settle any differences between ASM.JS/WASM and C/C++. What you're saying is that it's actually changing the behavior of the language in breaking ways - i.e. in this case it's removing short circuiting guarantees made by the C/C++ standards, making this a very dangerous option that should probably not be used on any non-trivial piece of code.

> E.g. from the C++ standard, 5.14.1:
> (The && operator groups left-to-right. The operands are both contextually converted to type bool (Clause 4). The result is true if both operands are true and false otherwise. **Unlike &, && guarantees left-to-right evaluation: the second operand is not evaluated if the first operand is false.**

I guess for us it just means we turn this flag off, but you might want to make the comment in settings a bit more explicit about it breaking the standard, giving more warning to potential users that this flag is likely to cause perfectly valid code to fail unexpectedly :)

Can you comment a bit more on what the intended use cases for this flag were and what we're losing out on by not using it?

Thanks again!

---

[kripken]: >  it's removing short circuiting guarantees made by the C/C++ standards, making this a very dangerous option that should probably not be used on any non-trivial piece of code.

Correct - this flag is **not** safe in general. It simply tells the binaryen optimizer "nothing will trap, ever" (except for an explicit `unreachable` instruction, but nothing implicit). So as you said, it is not safe for general C/C++ code, you must be very careful in using it.

Note that it doesn't break the `&&` semantics in a general sense - we still handle side effects, that is, `f() && g()` will not unconditionally do both calls. The only change is that we assume there are no implicit traps, which means we ignore a specific set of side effects. In this case, we assume that loads have no side effects.

You aren't missing much by not enabling this feature - maybe a percent or so of code, last I checked. That's why it's off by default, and we don't recommend people enable it. But there are small/simple codebases where it is helpful and every byte matters.

---

[kripken]: And thanks, yes, the docs were not clear enough. I opened #8957 for that.

title: glGetString crashes when called on a lost context
body:
`gl.getSupportedExtensions()` returns null when the context is lost, but emscripten's WebGL code doesn't check for null first before using it. This is showing up in our error logs as crashes in our application. These crashes are bad because they corrupt our application state (by not running destructors on the stack).

From a quick code search, this happens in these places:

https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/blob/1e355f97d28510c7e4b02dbe7169e474c6cf717b/src/library_webgl2.js#L32-L34

https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/blob/2b3e0b81a8d02cc3a735d942d5d450fb0140ec7f/src/library_webgl.js#L533-L538

https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/blob/ecff8a02919a5253e096fae94f9f57f766931d8c/src/library_glemu.js#L255

The first one is the one we're hitting, but all of them should probably be fixed. Here's a proof of concept demonstrating that this value can be null:

```js
> c = document.createElement('canvas')
> gl = c.getContext('webgl')
> gl.getExtension('WEBGL_lose_context').loseContext()
> gl.getSupportedExtensions()
null
```
comments:
[juj]: Fixed in above commit.

---

[juj]: Note that context loss handling is not really well tested at all - you are likely to run into other issues as well around this area, bug reports welcome.

title: Regression bug: Relative import of ES6 WASM modules from ES6 Modules does not work
body:
Regression bug introduced by the PR #8940 related to the bug #8729.

Problem :
The PR is based on the fact that 'document.currentScript.src' exists in ES6 modules.
This is not the case for VanillaJS ( no magic bundling ) for Firefox>=68 and Chrome>=76.

This causes any import of ES6 module which is not in the same directory that the source html file to fail.

Reproduce :

    Generate a ES6 WASM + js hello_world in a subdirectory
    Create a parent main.html page + main.js vanillaJS ES6 module in a parent directory
    Import the hello_world from the main.js.
    It will fail: The hello_world.js will not succeed to fetch the WASM file.

Temporary Fix :

Override the "locateFile" in the Module itself with a callback that enforce the WASM module path

Definitive Fix:
Enforce the usage of PTHREAD and WebWorker is not a good solution considering that this support is disable in almost all the main WebBrowser for now.

I would be for adding a flag to disable "import.meta.url" on demand. And enable it by default for ANY ES6_MODULE.

title: embind serialization of string to std::wstring fails if memory growth happens
body:
I'm getting a weird bug where sending a string from JS to C++ using embind fails if the string is really big. The string is the right size but the contents are random, as if it had never been initialized. The bug is in `embind_register_std_wstring`:

https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/blob/b42d1b3c5c136e94071d9ca10c660a410426ffcc/src/embind/embind.js#L755-L769

This code incorrectly calls `getHeap()` before calling `_malloc()`. If `_malloc()` causes the heap to grow, then the heap reference obtained earlier is stale. This then causes the code below to write past the end of the old array, which goes nowhere. The memory for the string remains uninitialized.

This is basically the same issue as #3299. I'm filing it as a new issue because that one's really old. It appears that this bug has been around for quite a long time since this buggy code is from #3318 (so since 2015).

Sorry, I don't have time to put together a patch. It should be an easy fix though.

title: Build regression: "STANDALONE_WASM does not support memory growth yet"
body:
The following command line used to work a few months ago - I think this was with 1.38.40:

`
emcc src/vertexcodec.cpp src/indexcodec.cpp -O3 -DNDEBUG -s EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS='["_meshopt_decodeVertexBuffer", "_meshopt_decodeIndexBuffer"]' -s ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH=1 -s TOTAL_STACK=24576 -s TOTAL_MEMORY=65536 -o build/meshopt_decoder.wasm
`

After uprading to 1.38.47, I now get the following error:

`
shared:ERROR: STANDALONE_WASM does not support memory growth yet
`

Memory growth worked correctly before the update. Any pointers as to how to fix this would be appreciated.
comments:
[kripken]: This is because we are moving to a more robust approach for `-o X.wasm`. Before we just didn't emit the JS, and hoped for the best. After, we have the new `STANDALONE_WASM` mode which builds slightly different system libs etc., in order to get a working wasm file. And I added some assertions for things known to not work yet.

Did the output you got before actually work, including memory growth? How did you run it, and with what support code (specifically, what handled the growth)?

If there was stuff that worked before that the assertions now prevent, we should remove them, but would be good to understand what that was.

---

[zeux]: > Did the output you got before actually work, including memory growth? How did you run it, and with what support code (specifically, what handled the growth)?

Yeah the output before worked without issues; the memory growth support code I used was simply resizing the Memory object - note that the C++ code in question doesn't do any memory allocations, so this function is called from JS:

https://github.com/zeux/meshoptimizer/blob/master/js/meshopt_decoder.js#L13-L21

Just removing this check in the new emscripten build isn't sufficient for getting this to work though - not sure why yet.

---

[kripken]: I see, thanks!

My guess is it doesn't work now because you provide `sbrk`, but we changed that ABI. `sbrk` is now internal in the wasm module (to make it more standalone). Instead, it imports a simpler `emscripten_resize_heap` function that is called to resize. To see more, I'd look at the imports, with something like `wasm-dis X.wasm | grep import` (but the wasm VM should also error and tell you what's missing on the import object, when it instantiates).

Another difference is that the wasm will create the memory itself, you don't need to create it on the outside and import it (again, this makes the wasm more standalone).

Sorry for the confusion, but this is an internal ABI detail that we don't guarantee won't change, and we had to optimize now.

That assertion was definitely unnecessary though, I'll remove it in #9588.

---

[zeux]: Yeah - I figured out how to adjust my code to make it work.

It looks like before, `memory` was an *import* so my JS wrapper had to provide it when loading the wasm module.
Now it's an *export* so I need to get it from the instance after loading.

I understand that I'm playing fast & loose here and I'm happy to adjust my code a bit after Emscripten releases - I couldn't find another way to get a small compact binary.

---

[zeux]: Interestingly I no longer need to supply "emscripten_memcpy_big" anymore either - I am assuming that the standalone version of libc now handles the copy internally without calling out to JS?

---

[kripken]: Correct, in standalone mode we don't expect JS to be able to do a super-fast memcpy for us, so it's all internal in the wasm.

---

[zeux]: Ok - thanks! The .wasm file is a touch bigger with the new standalone mode, but it evens out with the reductions in the JS blob (.wasm is embedded into .js here):

-rwxrwxrwx 1 zeux zeux 8407 Oct  6 19:06 meshopt_decoder.js
-rwxrwxrwx 1 zeux zeux 3865 Oct  6 19:06 meshopt_decoder.js.gz
-rwxrwxrwx 1 zeux zeux 8346 Oct  6 19:04 meshopt_decoder_new.js
-rwxrwxrwx 1 zeux zeux 3839 Oct  6 19:04 meshopt_decoder_new.js.gz

My code did depend on memcpy but the sizes were below the old JS threshold so performance isn't affected here either, which is great.

---

[zeux]: ... in fact, it looks like with the new runtime I can even export sbrk via `-s EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS` which means I no longer need a JS stub for heap management. A JS implementation of sbrk used to be valuable for code size reasons, since the C implementation of sbrk would require a lot of odd imports such as DYNAMICTOP_PTR, but now all of this is self-contained inside the .wasm - which is great because it simplifies the implementation of the JS wrapper. So as far as I can tell, memory growth for standalone mode "just works" with no need for any imports/exports.

title: Pthread assert on exit
body:
I'm hitting an assertion in `terminateAllThreads` when my app exits.

Specifically this one:

https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/blob/9f883dc1f197541ac5c49a8653e7a5a1af63a099/src/library_pthread.js#L228

It may be my misunderstanding, but it seems strange to assert that the pthread will exist when there is code above this that goes through every pthread and sets them all to null.

Is this a bug in the JS, or am I doing something wrong?

My configuration looks like:

```
-s USE_PTHREADS

-s EXIT_RUNTIME
-s DISABLE_EXCEPTION_CATCHING=0
```

title: Promise' is undefined
body:
I just upgraded from 1.35.0 to 1.39.2 with CMake on MACOs and found out that the web assembly formate is not supported by IE so I linked with -s WASM=0. I then got the error about polyfills which I fixed with -s LEGACY_VM_SUPPORT=1. Now I get the following output in the console:

DOM7011: The code on this page disabled back and forward caching. For more information, see: http://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=291337
SoftAdmin.htm
HTML1300: Navigation occurred.
goglobal
DOM7011: The code on this page disabled back and forward caching. For more information, see: http://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=291337
SoftAdmin.htm
init http://dave16.graphon.com/goglobal/?useapp=false
SCRIPT5009: 'Promise' is undefined
webappcore.js (477939,3)
still waiting on run dependencies:
dependency: wasm-instantiate
(end of list)
still waiting on run dependencies:
dependency: wasm-instantiate
(end of list)


The last part just keeps repeating. I tried adding Promise with -s EXTRA_EXPORTED_RUNTIME_METHODS=\"['ccall', 'UTF8ToString', 'Promise']\" but that just caused the linker to complain with:

invalid item (maybe a typo?) in EXPORTED_RUNTIME_METHODS: Promise

Google was no help. What am I doing wrong?
comments:
[sbc100]: Promise is an ES6 feature which is looks like emscripten depends on.     If we want to continue to support IE and ES5 we should probably work around our use of Promises here and/or have a better transpile story.

 What line is the Promise reference coming from?  Most of our use of promises seems to be around wasm loading so I would hope that non-wasm use of emscripten might still be able to avoid using them.

---

[73UJ34]: I did add -s WASM=0, but the console output implies that wasm is attempting to be loaded. Here's the code chunk with the error being the new Promise at the bottom.

function getBinaryPromise() {
  // if we don't have the binary yet, and have the Fetch api, use that
  // in some environments, like Electron's render process, Fetch api may be present, but have a different context than expected, let's only use it on the Web
  if (!wasmBinary && (ENVIRONMENT_IS_WEB || ENVIRONMENT_IS_WORKER) && typeof fetch === 'function') {
    return fetch(wasmBinaryFile, { credentials: 'same-origin' }).then(function(response) {
      if (!response['ok']) {
        throw "failed to load wasm binary file at '" + wasmBinaryFile + "'";
      }
      return response['arrayBuffer']();
    }).catch(function () {
      return getBinary();
    });
  }
  // Otherwise, getBinary should be able to get it synchronously
  return new Promise(function(resolve, reject) {
    resolve(getBinary());
  });
}

This works fine in Chrome and FF.

---

[73UJ34]: Here is a simple test app that reproduces the problem (the DEBUG files are included):
[Promise.zip](https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/files/3866034/Promise.zip)

---

[kripken]: I think we should add a little Promise polyfill when `LEGACY_VM_SUPPORT` is enabled.

This is a regression in upstream, as in upstream we use wasm2js and implement the non-wasm output in as wasm a manner as possible, using the same APIs. That's a simpler model than the old asm.js support. But it does mean we end up using a Promise in one place.

---

[73UJ34]: How long will it take for this fix to get into a stable release? Our next release is scheduled for Q1.

---

[kripken]: Once there is a PR, we can probably merge that in in a matter of days, and we tag a release every week or so. So it should be well before Q1, assuming someone has time to open a PR for it.

Maybe you're interested to do that? If so let me know if there's any questions about the process that I can help with!

---

[embeddedt]: Should the polyfill be part of Emscripten itself? Wouldn't it make more sense to have people include a Promise polyfill themselves if necessary? Lots of other projects take the second approach.

The problem I see with providing a built-in polyfill is that when everyone polyfills the features they need, the resulting bundle of code contains a lot of duplicate implementations of the same thing. Using one global, standards-compliant polyfill is better for code size (in my experience) than including many different polyfills in different locations.

It also eases the burden on migration: shrinking bundle size by removing/reducing polyfills can become as simple as removing one global `import`, instead of turning off polyfilling for many different components.

I'm not trying to change the plan here: just trying to get a sense of which way would be preferable.

---

[sbc100]: How about this:

1. Drop all support for ES5 and LEGACY_VM_SUPPORT from emscripten
2. Add support for running bable as post-link phase for those who really needs ES5
3. Find some way to do some minimal amount of testing for IE

TBH I would have imagined that those targeting IE/ES5 would already have a transpiler like that in their build process so (2) might not be necessary, but it would be nice to integrate it if only for our testing purposes.

---

[bvibber]: My main concern with not including the Promise polyfill in the direct output from emscripten is that if you do `emcc -s WASM=0 -s LEGACY_VM_SUPPORT=1 -o foo.html foo.c` you won't get something that works in IE 11.

Perhaps it belongs in the shell, as equivalent of the top-level application?

---

[sbc100]: What if LEGACY_VM_SUPPORT=1 means we run babel on the output (as a post-link step within emscripten itself) to convert to ES5?

---

[73UJ34]: I'm guessing that a PR is a Pull Request, but I'm not sure what that entails. Are you suggesting that I try to fix this myself? Seeing as how I don't even know what a Promise is I doubt I will be much help.

---

[kripken]: @sbc100 I think it's useful to keep our output working by default without post-processing tools. Yes, if we run babel ourselves (like we do closure) that would be a way to do that. But that's a large change that we should consider separately. One specific issue to consider is I'm not sure `LEGACY_VM_SUPPORT` is implementable as a post-processing pass that just adds code, as it may modify our codegen. 

I think adding a short Promise polyfill when LEGACY_VM_SUPPORT is on is a good solution for now. Our Promise usage is very minimal, so the polyfill might be just a few lines.

@73UJ34 I see, no worries. Hopefully someone else has time for this soon. If not I can probably get to it by the end of the year, so it should be before your deadline.

---

[sbc100]: I agree with the fact at that we should keep our code working.   However I think it seems reasonable that if you are in the tiny minority who need `LEGACY_VM_SUPPORT` that you should have to install babel in order for the build to succeed.    Does requiring babel to be installed if you want to use `LEGACY_VM_SUPPORT` seem like too much to ask?

I agree its a larger change and won't block a more minimal fix, but I'd still like to know if you think this is a reasonable longer term fix?

---

[73UJ34]: Thank you all for your attention to this problem. If it does not get fixed in time we have the option to go back to using emscripten 1.35.0. Thanks again.

---

[kripken]: @sbc100 I guess I'm not sure. It depends on how easy it would be for people to install babel and get emcc to use it properly.

---

[embeddedt]: >  It depends on how easy it would be for people to install babel and get emcc to use it properly.

I suppose you could either get `emcc` to run something along the lines of `npx babel`, or even just `require()` Babel (like a bundler would). Either way, Babel is pretty straightforward to install so I don't think it would be that much extra work for users.

Is Babel necessary for this, though? We're not trying to transpile new syntax; we are just polyfilling a new feature. Babel itself doesn't provide polyfills; it can just optionally add import statements for them at the top of a file.

---

[sbc100]: I'd like to be able to use ES6 features (such as Promises) freely in emscripten, and have a tool transpile it down to ES5.  I thought babel did that?    If its not babel we can just the choose whatever the best tool is to doing this.  Trying to ah-hoc monkey patch our own ES6 feature implementation seems like the wrong approach in the long run.

---

[embeddedt]: > I'd like to be able to use ES6 features (such as Promises) freely in emscripten, and have a tool transpile it down to ES5. I thought babel did that? If its not babel we can just the choose whatever the best tool is to doing this.

If you want full ES6 support on ES5 platforms, you need two things:

* A transpiler (i.e. Babel) for converting ES6 syntax (`i => i +1`) to ES5 syntax (`function(i) { return i + 1; }`).
* Polyfills for ES6 features (like `Object.assign`, `Promise`, etc.).

---

[sbc100]: I see.  My point is really the IIUC these are will understood problems in the JS space that have good existing solutions, right?

---

[embeddedt]: > these are [sic] will understood problems in the JS space that have good existing solutions, right?

Yes. Generally speaking, the program that outputs the final JS/HTML file is the one responsible for downlevelling everything. In this case I suppose that would be `emcc`, so I guess `emcc` needs to add the ability to run Babel and/or include `core-js` (the de facto polyfill).

title: errno.h constants regression (wasi types vs preprocessor)
body:
As of cffcd70471ad158028992a70fdae890ea415970d the definitions of `EPERM` etc in `errno.h` changed from untyped integers to typed references to wasi constants, such as:

```c
#define EPERM              __WASI_ERRNO_PERM
...
#define __WASI_ERRNO_PERM ((__wasi_errno_t)63)
```

This breaks preprocessor code like this in the dav1d AV1 decoder:

```c
#if EPERM > 0
#define DAV1D_ERR(e) (-(e)) ///< Negate POSIX error code.
#else
#define DAV1D_ERR(e) (e)
#endif
```

Test case:

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <errno.h>

#if EPERM > 0
#endif

int main(int argc, const char **argv) {
    printf("Hello, world\n");
    return 0;
}
```

```

title: Fix embinding functions for wasm backend
body:
Embinding functions for wasm backend doesn't always work because of missing `dynCall_` signatures. This is because the wasm backend doesn't support function pointer bitcasting, and has a pass that generates bitcast thunks to wrap the type signatures. s2wasm knows which `dynCall_` functions to generate based on the symbols it can find - specifically as relocations in `wasm-linker`.

The problem is fundamentally that by bitcasting function types we're hiding the type information. So, let's just not bitcast.

The solution I have here is to use `void*` instead of `void (*)(void)` as the interchange type between JS and C++. This is fine because JS has its own notion of what types mean, the actual bits of the function pointer that crosses the JS-wasm boundary are the same. `void*` says on the C++ side that we don't care about the type of the pointer, which is closer to how JS sees it.

Tested with `default`, `asm2`, and `binaryen2` (using both asm2wasm and s2wasm). Tried testing `other.test_embind` but that's broken on `incoming`
comments:
[kripken]: > This is because the wasm backend doesn't support function pointer bitcasting

What does that mean?

---

[jgravelle-google]: Er, more accurately, *wasm* doesn't support function pointer aliasing, i.e. `call_indirect` is strongly typed.

So, given C code:
```c
int foo(int x, float y) {
  return 2 * x;
}
int bar() {
  int (*f)(int) = (int (*)(int))foo;
  return foo(2);
}
```
we would naively generate something like `call_indirect foo 2 (with type ii)`, which would be a runtime validation error.
So the wasm backend changes `bar` into something like:
```c
int bar() {
  int (*f)(int) = bitcast_1;
  return f(2);
}
int bitcast_1(int x) {
  return foo(x, 0);
}
```

The problem then being that if `foo` was the only function with its signature (`iif`), we no longer take the address of any functions that match it, and when we try to call `dynCall_iif` we haven't generated it.

---

[kripken]: Hmm, so that is the same problem in asm.js too (without the optional function type emulation), your C example would fail there too. But embind does work in asm.js..?

---

[jgravelle-google]: For embind we would do the function pointer casting to pass the function to javascript, so we would never try to call the casted pointer directly in asm.js, and it would work out. Instead we would pass the pointer to a `dynCall_` function which would look it up in a function table.
For asm.js we generate the `dynCall_` functions as part of the JSBackend, for wasm backend they're generated in `s2wasm`, after the bitcast function generation.
The problem is we have something like `void embind_in_js(void (*fptr)(void));`, which `dynCall`s the pointer in JS library code. So the real type signature escapes the module, and we then expect the module to know about the type signature. That we do this is out-of-band knowledge that `s2wasm` can't really have. And we can avoid it entirely by changing the signature declaration to `void embind_in_js(void *fptr);`

---

[kripken]: I see now, thanks. Ok, overall this looks like a reasonable thing in general. @AlexPerrot, do you have any concerns with this change to embind?

title: WIP: Fix function pointer calls with new signatures in side modules
body:
I seem to be encountering a bug in emulated function pointer calls.

If a `SIDE_MODULE` makes a function pointer call (even internally) and that function has a signature that isn't present in the `MAIN_MODULE`, it ends up calling `invoke_X` which fails with:

```
TypeError: cannot pass i64 to or from JS
invoke_X()@https://extremely-alpha.iodide.app/pyodide-0.4.0/pyodide.asm.js:8:690227
```

I'm not exactly sure why we hit this particular message, since the function itself doesn't have any i64 arguments, but clearly the generic wasm function calling approach in `invoke_X` is failing us here.

The solution that's working for me is to generate a closure that calls the underlying `dynCall_...` function rather than doing the very most generic thing that `invoke_X` does.

All of this was discovered in Pyodide, but I'm struggling to produce a minimal example.  This requires that the generated wasm includes calls to the Javascript `invoke_` function, which happens in the context of Pyodide, but not in my minimal example.  Is there some flag or scenario that triggers the generation of `call $invoke_...`?
comments:
[kripken]: `invoke_*` functions are used for 2 things: C++ exceptions and setjmp. For setjmp, any indirect call in a function with a setjmp will use an invoke (even if the setjmp is not called, but so long as the optimizer did not remove it). That might be the easiest way to get a small testcase here.

title: Port sanitizer stack traces to emscripten
body:
This allows the stack trace mechanism in sanitizers to work with emscripten.

### Example

Consider `null-read.c`:

```c
int main(void) {
    int *a = 0, b;
    b = *a;
}
```

Let's compile it with UBSan, enable debug info, turn on stack trace printing by changing the environment:

```console
$ emcc -g4 -fsanitize=null null-read.c
$ perl -pi -e "s/(?<=ENV=){}/{'UBSAN_OPTIONS': 'print_stacktrace=1'}/" a.out.js
```

Stack traces display properly on all major engines:

```console
$ node a.out.js 
null-read.c:3:9: runtime error: load of null pointer of type 'int'
    #0 0x21005d in __original_main wasm-function[33]:93
    #1 0x220003 in main wasm-function[34]:3
$ d8 a.out.js 
null-read.c:3:9: runtime error: load of null pointer of type 'int'
    #0 0x21005d in __original_main wasm-function[33]:93
    #1 0x220003 in main wasm-function[34]:3
$ sm a.out.js 
null-read.c:3:9: runtime error: load of null pointer of type 'int'
    #0 0x73c in __original_main /<redacted>/null-read.c:3:9
    #1 0x76c in main /<redacted>/null-read.c:4:1
    #2 0x80001822 in Module._main a.out.js:6178:32
    #3 0x80001917 in callMain a.out.js:6423:22
    #4 0x80001951 in doRun a.out.js:6481:49
    #5 0x8000195f in run a.out.js:6495:5
    #6 0x80001900 in runCaller a.out.js:6400:29
    #7 0x800005e4 in removeRunDependency a.out.js:1508:7
    #8 0x800006af in receiveInstance a.out.js:1711:5
    #9 0x800006c1 in receiveInstantiatedSource/< a.out.js:1729:5
```

Due to [v8 bug 9262](https://bugs.chromium.org/p/v8/issues/detail?id=9262), we cannot display the actual source file and line numbers on `d8` and `node`.

title: Fix memory leak in Chrome - Error objects do not like to be persistent
body:
Fix memory leak in Chrome - Error objects do not like to be persistent, they seem to heavily capture variables they have in their scope.

In Chrome, calling `var x = new Error();` in global scope causes an immediate capture of the scope, which leads in `Module` being captured, along with `.data`, `.wasm`, `.mem` etc. raw byte arrays, never reclaiming the memory.

I don't think there's any pressing reason for ExitStatus  to inherit from Error anyways? (was it due to convenience to get a pretty-printed error callstack?)

title: Wrong path for tflite.wasm
body: I'm trying to add the virtual background to an angular 11 project and getting an error when trying to load the tflite model:```GET http://localhost:4200/tflite.wasm 404 (Not Found)tflite.js:9 wasm streaming compile failed: TypeError: Failed to execute 'compile' on 'WebAssembly': HTTP status code is not oktflite.js:9 falling back to ArrayBuffer instantiationGET http://localhost:4200/tflite.wasm 404 (Not Found)failed to asynchronously prepare wasm: RuntimeError: abort(both async and sync fetching of the wasm failed). Build with -s ASSERTIONS=1 for more info.```This is how I import tflite.js:```javascriptimport createTFLiteModule from './tflite/tflite';import createTFLiteSIMDModule from './tflite/tflite-simd';```The path to tflite.wasm is hardcoded in tflite/tflite.js. Is there a config option to set the path without modifying tflite.js?```javascriptvar wasmBinaryFile="tflite.wasm"```
comments: ["I hope there is a way to import wasm module using ES modules like you did but I haven't found the right way to do it. So what I did in this demo was to put `tflite.js` and `tflite.wasm` in the public directory (aka `assets` in Angular); manually added the required `<script>` tags in [`index.html`](https://github.com/Volcomix/virtual-background/blob/c367b96ba0fc2213a9ff262dde06e352754b5288/public/index.html#L46) and manually declared [`createTFLiteModule`](https://github.com/Volcomix/virtual-background/blob/c367b96ba0fc2213a9ff262dde06e352754b5288/src/core/hooks/useTFLite.ts#L7) for TypeScript to be happy when calling it without any associated `import`.====="; "I didn't find a way to set the path yet. Maybe we can add a global variable like TFLITE_URL and TFLITE_SIMD_URL that the js file will use if exists. Not sure if relevant.====="; "Actually `tflite.js` and `tflite.wasm` are generated by [emscripten](https://emscripten.org/) and the glue code in the js file is overwritten each time I build tflite in wasm. I don't think that would be a good idea to edit the file manually so unless there is an existing option in emscripten to specify the wasm file URL (which I can't find); I don't see any other alternative than importing those files from outside of the bundled code.====="; 'Relative path should work when loading tflite.js in a script tag because the glue code use [document.currentScript.url](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/currentScript). See https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/pull/5368```var _scriptDir = typeof document !== \'undefined\' && document.currentScript ? document.currentScript.src : undefined;```Angular dev server generate the html dynamically with <script src="app.js"></script>. That\'s why document.currentScript.url points to the root path.I think on dev we can add a proxy that handles the wasm files specifically. Maybe with "ng serve --proxy-config proxy.conf.json".On production; as long as the .js and wasm files will be in the same path it should work because of document.currentScript.url.====='; 'Maybe we need```-s EXPORT_ES6=1 will turn the JavaScript code into an ES6 module with a default export that works with any bundler. Also requires -s MODULARIZE=1 to be set.```====='; 'Running a build with this option (https://github.com/Volcomix/virtual-background/commit/cdad50c0f67c3537854c1b9ea6b8bef498b55fcc): https://github.com/Volcomix/virtual-background/actions/runs/890576517====='; "There is also [USE_ES6_IMPORT_META=1](https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/blob/main/src/settings.js#L1166):// Use the ES6 Module relative import feature 'import.meta.url'// to auto-detect WASM Module path.// It might not be supported on old browsers / toolchainsvar USE_ES6_IMPORT_META = 1;====="; "I updated tflite js files in [this branch](https://github.com/Volcomix/virtual-background/tree/emscripten-es6-export). React is yelling at me when trying to import them as ES6 modules:![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7324857/120114117-ead78e00-c17d-11eb-9163-4db3e29a0313.png)But maybe could you have more luck with Angular.USE_ES6_IMPORT_META is enabled by default so I'm gonna run a new build with this option disabled.====="; "I'm getting a similar error with Angular 11. EXPORT_ES6=1 with import.model.url is probably the solution but react and angular tooling are not compatible with import.model yet.====="; "I still prefer the automatic import.model.url solution but we can also pass custom [locateFile function](https://emscripten.org/docs/api_reference/module.html#Module.locateFile):```javascriptconst createdTFLiteSIMD = await createTFLiteModule({locateFile: () => 'path/to//tflite.wasm'});```====="; 'Still an error with `"-s USE_ES6_IMPORT_META=0"`:![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7324857/121773236-ce265780-cb7a-11eb-813e-1f61045b2b27.png)====='; 'Not sure about complication flags but we can use locateFile to dynamically specify the model location.This is from the [Selfie Segmentation example](https://google.github.io/mediapipe/solutions/selfie_segmentation#javascript-solution-api):```javascriptconst selfieSegmentation = new SelfieSegmentation({locateFile: (file) => { return `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@mediapipe/selfie_segmentation/${file}`;}});```=====']
